summary: The study explores the use of atomic layer deposition (ALD) to create NiO thin films as oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrocatalysts. The ALD process uses Ni(Cp)2 and O3 as precursors at 275 °C. The incorporation of Fe from the electrolyte significantly enhances the catalytic activity of the NiO films. The Fe content in the electrolyte affects the electrochemical performance, with Fe-saturated electrolytes leading to higher turnover frequencies (TOF) and improved stability. The study highlights the importance of pretreatment and electrolyte conditioning in optimizing the activity and surface area of ALD-deposited NiO films for OER.
